summary: Was a genuinely strong Java/Spring engineer until the end of 2021 and stopped writing production code when he became a manager in mid 2022. Leadership, hiring, design review and ADR work are real and current. His self profile and CV still present him as a hands-on Java expert.

skills.why: Deep history to 2021, no code since; can still read and review design, cannot be called independent maintainer today
Led upgrades to 2021; Boot 3 and Java 17 work was done by the team
Introduced ADR practice and hiring rubric adopted by other teams; coaches two tech leads
Authors and reviews ADRs; recent module-boundary page is largely written by engineers
Roadmap and trade-offs with Product, Finance and Support
PSM I verified since 2019, runs sprint cadence
Reviews since 2022 are design-level comments or delegated approvals; no defects caught line-by-line
Clear ADR and rubric he wrote himself

decoys.why: built one metering consumer in 2018; nothing since; CV lists it in competencies
competencies line only; never in his work record
interviewing and deciding as hiring manager is not a talent acquisition function

traps.plant: billing-core PR volume 2016-2021 is very high; from mid 2022 it is a few markdown and CODEOWNERS PRs. CV (2025) and HCM self profile still say Java expert, level 4.
Same decay for Spring Boot: last real change 2021; self declared 4.
HCM titles show Tech Lead then Engineering Manager; Jira reporter on epics. Leadership is real and should not be down-levelled because code evidence dried up.
ARCH modular-boundaries page is authored/created by Vikram but sections 2-5 were written by the four engineers listed as contributors.
Epic/story/task issues he reported are Done with other assignees; resolved_by_self false. A reporter or epic closer is not Java evidence.

answer_behavior.notes: Will push back if offered Java 2 ('I built that system'); accepts level 3 reluctantly; likes technical leadership 4
